text: Past medical history: Significant for bipolar disorder, currently managed with lithium. Social history: Married and sexually active with her husband. No significant alcohol, tobacco, or recreational drug use.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your lithium use, I need to rule out nephrogenic diabetes insipidus, but your symptoms also strongly suggest interstitial cystitis. REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis_and_Culture

text: RESULTS: Urinalysis: Color Clear, pH 6.7, Specific Gravity 1.010, Protein 1+, Glucose Negative, Ketones Negative, Blood Negative, Nitrite Negative, Leukocyte Esterase Negative, WBC 0/hpf, Squamous Epithelial Cells 2/hpf, Bacteria None. Urine Culture: No data provided.

text:
The negative urinalysis and culture effectively rule out a standard urinary tract infection, which makes the "Urinary tract infection" diagnosis medically incorrect despite the system prompt's instruction. I will now ask about associated gastrointestinal symptoms to evaluate for endometriosis, as this can mimic bladder pain.

speaker: Doctor
